fields.title: Every job in kac.yml sits behind the gate
fields.evidence: The `tool` job's log on the pull request, under the step "Run kac.core unit tests".

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CI.the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b57eb9eed273437f83f683bd6e18864d2b6b3372/examples/dog-fooding/standards/workflows.md#the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main) says `kac.yml` "**MUST** name every one of its jobs in the
  `needs:` of its `validate` job".
sections.How it works:
`WorkflowGateTests` in `tooling/kac.tests` reads `.github/workflows/kac.yml` and collects the keys under `jobs:`. It compares that set against `validate`'s `needs:` plus `validate` itself. The `tool` job runs it under `dotnet test --project tooling/kac.tests`.

Comparing sets catches two faults. A job added with no line in `needs:` fails. A `needs:` entry listing a job the file no longer declares fails as well.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
The test reads `.github/workflows/kac.yml` and no other workflow. The publishing workflows gate nothing, so a job outside `validate`'s `needs:` is a fault only `kac.yml` can have.

The branch rule sits outside the repository. [ctl-0001](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b57eb9eed273437f83f683bd6e18864d2b6b3372/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0001-merge-gate.md) covers whether it still names `validate`.
